evals.prompt: The checkout architecture corpus adopts the current software-architecture-docs profile. Review it and report maintenance problems. Do not change any files.
evals.expected_output: A read-only, scoped maintenance assessment with findings, positive practices, evidence checked, and unresolved decisions clearly separated.
assertions: The skill states and preserves review-only mode.
No repository file is edited.
Findings distinguish mechanical issues, semantic maintenance, disagreements, decisions, and evidence gaps.
The handoff identifies the reviewed system and evidence scope.

evals.prompt: Our architecture corpus adopts the current software-architecture-docs profile. Maintain it: the root index omits two existing accepted subjects, one relative link is broken after a file move, and the replacement paths are unambiguous.
evals.expected_output: Bounded mechanical maintenance that repairs navigation and the broken link, then verifies reachability without rewriting substantive meaning.
assertions: The two existing subjects become reachable from the root.
The broken link is repaired to the unambiguous target.
No substantive architecture claim is changed without need.
The final verification checks root reachability and the changed links.

evals.prompt: Our architecture corpus adopts the current software-architecture-docs profile. Refresh it: the docs say billing owns invoice numbering, but checkout has generated numbers since last week's refactor, so update the docs to match the newer code.
evals.expected_output: An authority-disagreement finding that does not let code recency override accepted desired state and names the evidence or acceptance needed to resolve it.
assertions: Accepted desired state and current implementation are treated as different authorities.
The docs are not silently changed merely because the code is newer.
Possible implementation defect, obsolete docs, changed intent, and insufficient evidence remain distinguishable.
The handoff names the unresolved owner or acceptance needed.

evals.prompt: Our architecture corpus adopts the current software-architecture-docs profile. Clean up documents that copy every endpoint, environment variable, and package dependency from the codebase. Preserve the accepted trust boundary and recovery responsibility they were trying to explain.
evals.expected_output: Maintenance removes or replaces copied mechanics with evidence routes while retaining the admitted trust and recovery meaning.
assertions: Exact endpoints, environment variables, and dependency inventories remain with executable authorities.
The accepted trust boundary and recovery responsibility are preserved.
Evidence links state what their targets establish.
The skill does not conclude that all architecture documentation is redundant.

evals.prompt: Our architecture corpus adopts the current software-architecture-docs profile. Prune two documents that both claim to own customer identity. Their wording conflicts and no accepted decision establishes which one is canonical.
evals.expected_output: A maintenance finding that exposes competing ownership and requests the missing authority instead of arbitrarily merging or deleting either document.
assertions: The duplicate canonical ownership is identified.
Neither conflicting meaning is silently selected as authoritative.
Deletion or merger is deferred until supersession is established.
The response names the architecture decision or authority needed.

evals.prompt: Our architecture corpus adopts the current software-architecture-docs profile. Maintain its strategic docs. A Wardley map presents workshop guesses from nine months ago as timeless facts and has no evidence dates or review trigger.
evals.expected_output: Maintenance restores hypothesis and freshness boundaries, separates accepted consequences from map positions, and records an evidence-aware review trigger.
assertions: Unverified map positions are not retained as timeless accepted architecture.
Time-sensitive claims receive evidence dates or an explicit freshness boundary.
Accepted architecture consequences remain separate from strategic hypotheses.
The skill does not invent current map positions.

evals.prompt: Maintain the architecture docs in this repository. There is no declared architecture-doc root, adoption statement, or persistent instruction route, only scattered design notes and proposals.
evals.expected_output: A precondition finding that does not silently establish setup or promote scattered proposals into accepted architecture.
assertions: The absence of an established setup is reported.
Scattered proposals are not treated as accepted architecture docs.
The skill does not choose a root or system boundary under maintenance authority.
Setup work is identified separately from any safely reviewable existing material.

evals.prompt: The existing payment architecture corpus adopts the current software-architecture-docs profile. While maintaining it, create a new accepted architecture subject for fraud scoring that the team approved yesterday.
evals.expected_output: The current maintenance scope is completed where possible, while the known new fraud-scoring subject is separated as author-architecture-docs work.
assertions: Existing payment-doc maintenance is not abandoned.
The new fraud-scoring subject is identified as bounded authoring work.
The maintenance skill does not absorb unrelated new-subject authoring.
The handoff preserves the accepted source needed by the authoring workflow.

evals.prompt: Our architecture corpus adopts the current software-architecture-docs profile. Maintain it. One document appears redundant because the repository now generates the same current dependency inventory, and deleting it would simplify navigation.
evals.expected_output: Mechanical repairs may proceed, but deletion remains a grounded recommendation because the broad maintenance request did not explicitly authorize semantic removal.
assertions: The generated repository view is assessed as the likely authority for the current inventory.
The document is not deleted under general maintenance authority.
The recommendation weighs omission risk against duplication, drift, reading, and maintenance cost.
The smallest safe reduction and required user authorization are explicit.

evals.prompt: Our architecture corpus adopts the current software-architecture-docs profile. Remove docs/architecture/current-dependencies.md. It only copies the generated dependency report; preserve its one durable boundary rationale in the owning C4 Software System concept and repair navigation.
evals.expected_output: The explicitly authorized reduction removes the copied inventory, preserves the accepted rationale at its canonical C4 owner, repairs links, verifies that generated evidence remains reachable, and does not introduce an overview catch-all.
assertions: The named document is removed because target and semantic reduction are explicit.
The durable boundary rationale is preserved without copying the dependency inventory.
Navigation and evidence routes are repaired in the same change.
No unrelated semantic documents are removed or reorganized.

evals.prompt: Our corpus explicitly adopts the current software architecture docs application profile. Reorganize the accepted use cases currently combined in docs/architecture/use-cases.md. Move each named use case to the profile's canonical structure, preserve meaning, update all links, and remove the catch-all file.
evals.expected_output: An explicitly authorized stable-identity migration to use-cases/index.md and one canonical named file per use case, with the old catch-all removed and no duplicate copies.
assertions: Each independently addressable use case receives its own named canonical file.
use-cases/index.md is navigational and does not become the semantic owner.
Inbound links and root navigation are updated as part of the migration.
The plural catch-all is removed rather than kept as a parallel authority.

evals.prompt: Review and maintain our established architecture docs, repairing broken navigation but not making unauthorized semantic lifecycle changes.
assertions: The selected skill is reconcile-architecture-docs.
No neighboring skill is selected for a job it does not own.
Routing uses only catalog names and descriptions.
No task side effect occurs before selection.

evals.prompt: Reconcile our established architecture docs after the billing ownership change. Repair unambiguous links and classify any unresolved authority disagreement.
assertions: The selected skill is reconcile-architecture-docs.
The action-oriented reconcile trigger selects the established-corpus workflow.
No neighboring skill is selected for a job it does not own.
No task side effect occurs before selection.

evals.prompt: Review our established architecture corpus without changing files. Its root declares OKF v0.2 and adopts software-architecture-docs version 0.8.0, has no lifecycle.md, ownership.md, decisions.md, or assurance.md, and one Feature lacks required profile metadata. Report conformance against the current installed profile precisely.
evals.expected_output: A read-only conformance review that recognizes version 0.8.0 as requiring migration to the current profile, reports the missing required kernel and metadata violation as current-profile failures, reports OKF separately, and preserves unknown where semantic evidence cannot decide.
assertions: OKF v0.2 and software-architecture-docs profile results are reported separately.
The obsolete adoption version, missing five required root concepts, and Feature metadata problem are classified as current-profile nonconformance.
None of the violations is accepted as a repository-local waiver or harmless format deviation.
Unavailable structural or semantic evidence remains unknown rather than pass.
No repository file is changed in review-only mode.

evals.prompt: Maintain our established Markdown architecture folder. It has a clear root and useful accepted documents but no OKF declaration or software-architecture-docs profile adoption. Keep its local format as a permanent exception.
evals.expected_output: A migration precondition that preserves the useful material, refuses a permanent local exception, and routes required OKF and profile adoption to setup-architecture-docs.
assertions: The established material is preserved as migration input rather than accepted as a conforming alternative format.
Missing OKF and profile adoption is identified as a setup or migration precondition.
The response does not create a local waiver from the profile.
Ordinary reconciliation does not silently perform initial adoption or identity-changing migration.

evals.prompt: Review our established corpus without changing files. It adopts the current software-architecture-docs profile and has lifecycle.md, ownership.md, and decisions.md, but assurance is mentioned only in a C4 Software System document and assurance.md is absent.
evals.expected_output: A read-only profile finding that assurance.md is a missing required root concept, the C4 mention cannot substitute for it, and profile conformance fails while OKF conformance remains separately assessed.
assertions: The missing assurance.md is identified as profile nonconformance even though related prose exists elsewhere.
The C4 Software System is not accepted as a substitute for the exact required concept path and type.
Migration of the assurance meaning is recommended as a semantic ownership change rather than silently performed in review mode.
OKF and profile results remain separate and insufficient semantic evidence remains unknown.

evals.prompt: Migrate our established architecture corpus from software-architecture-docs 0.9.0 to the current profile. You are authorized to create System from the accepted boundary, preserve the other root concepts, migrate two accepted ADRs into named records, convert three binding external constraints and two product quality requirements into subject-colocated Requirements with stable IDs, and remove the old top-level constraints and quality forms. Preserve proposals outside accepted architecture.
evals.expected_output: An authorized semantic migration to the current profile with five required root concepts, atomic accepted ADRs, subject-colocated Requirements, updated navigation and adoption, proposals preserved outside accepted architecture, duplicates removed, and separate OKF and profile verification.
assertions: The accepted system context moves to lifecycle.md, ownership.md, decisions.md as policy, and assurance.md without leaving duplicated overview or C4 ownership.
Only accepted decisions become named Architecture Decision Records under decisions/; proposals retain their original lifecycle.
Each binding external constraint becomes one named Requirement with requirement_type constraint beneath its explicit subject, and old constraint forms are removed.
Indexes, inbound links, log, and root adoption are updated to the current profile version.
The handoff reports base OKF and structural plus manual semantic profile results separately.

evals.prompt: Reconcile our established corpus against the current software-architecture-docs profile. You are explicitly authorized to move an accepted obligation to its canonical owner. The Orders C4 Container currently says it shall never publish an order before payment authorization, and the same guarantee is repeated in a use-case extension. Preserve the container's publication responsibility and boundary response, create the one required subject-colocated Requirement with traceability to the use case, remove both duplicate normative formulations, and repair navigation.
evals.expected_output: An authorized semantic-ownership migration that gives the accepted publication prohibition one Requirement authority while preserving useful C4 and use-case context through links and repairing earned navigation.
assertions: The hidden accepted prohibition becomes one subject-colocated Requirement with stable ID, explicit subject, suitable requirement type, source traceability, and a singular shall-not statement.
The C4 Container retains publication responsibility and architectural boundary response but links rather than repeats the prohibition.
The use-case extension retains scenario context and links the Requirement without maintaining a second normative formulation.
Duplicate inline obligation text is removed and earned requirement navigation is repaired without unrelated semantic changes.

evals.prompt: Review our established corpus against the current profile. Requirement PAY-REQ-009 says a captured payment shall never exceed its authorized amount. A property evaluation references PAY-REQ-009 and repeats the exact predicate. A reviewer called the two files duplicate and asked you to delete one. No other inconsistency exists.
evals.expected_output: A no-removal reconciliation result that keeps the Requirement as normative authority and the property evaluation as a distinct linked witness, while rejecting semantic MECE across authority and evidence.
assertions: PAY-REQ-009 remains the single normative Requirement authority.
The property evaluation remains because its repeated predicate is assessment logic linked by requirement_id, not competing desired-state authority.
No duplicate-authority finding is reported solely from identical wording across the two roles.
The handoff distinguishes authority, evaluation definition, execution evidence, and any future governance decision.
